title: Half of all neutron stars may be born as magnetars
freshness: Published in Nature Astronomy on 10 September 2026, within the 15-day freshness window.
excerpt: A new study suggests that roughly half of the dense stellar remnants called neutron stars may be born as magnetars — objects with extraordinarily powerful magnetic fields. That would make these extreme stars much more common than astronomers previously estimated.
whyItMatters: Magnetars may be far more common than astronomers thought. If roughly half of neutron stars are born with these extraordinarily powerful magnetic fields, magnetars could be a much more important source of the Universe’s brightest explosions and mysterious radio flashes than previous estimates suggested.
